title: Research
description: Research by Frederic Hanusch: the planetarities as a new research field on planetary change and planetary politics, with research areas and projects.
intro: My work develops the planetarities as a new research field that engages with planetary change, and investigates planetary politics in particular.

Societies do not live on but are part of a planet. As the planet is ever-changing, so too are the relations societies create with it. My contribution centers on three key areas: the planetary itself, the methods through which it becomes knowable, and planetary politics, from the concept of time to the future of democracy. I currently examine what politics might look like if the Earth itself could participate in it.

title: Teaching
description: Teaching by Frederic Hanusch at Justus Liebig University Giessen: M.Sc. modules on planetary thinking and planetary methods, earlier seminars, supervision.
intro: My teaching examines how the humanities and social sciences can understand, interpret, and respond to planetary change, and how planetary politics can be analyzed and designed through conceptual, methodological, and field-based inquiry.

At Justus Liebig University Giessen, I have built a sequence of MA-level modules that introduces students to planetary thinking, advances planetary methods, and translates conceptual work into empirical field inquiry. Since 2026, I have also been course director of the M.Sc. One Health.

title: Curriculum Vitae
description: Curriculum vitae of Frederic Hanusch, Professor of Planetary Change and Politics at Justus Liebig University Giessen: positions, service, education, grants.
intro: Frederic Hanusch is Professor of Planetary Change and Politics at Justus Liebig University Giessen. He develops the planetarities as a new research field that engages with planetary change, and investigates planetary politics in particular.

He is co-founder and director of the Panel on Planetary Thinking, course director of the M.Sc. One Health, and a member of the British Academy and Carnegie Endowment working group on Transnational and Planetary Challenges. He reviews for journals including Nature Climate Change, Global Environmental Change and Earth System Governance, and for presses including MIT Press, Oxford University Press and the University of Chicago Press. He regularly appears in newspapers, on radio and on television.
